questions.q: Where should your most important headline numbers usually go on a dashboard?
options: In the bottom right corner
In a table at the very end
Hidden behind a View Report link
At the top left, as metric or gauge widgets
questions.explain: Readers scan from the top left, so headline metrics belong there.

questions.q: What should you do before adding any widgets to a new dashboard?
options: Add every available chart to see what fits
Decide the audience and the question the dashboard should answer
Turn on scheduled subscriptions
Create a dynamic dashboard
questions.explain: A one-sentence purpose statement keeps widgets that don't serve the audience off the page.

options: Sum of Amount by Stage
Chart 3
Open pipeline this quarter
Report output
questions.explain: A meaningful title with the timeframe reads faster than a raw measure and grouping name.

questions.q: How should you handle detail that only some viewers will want?
options: Lower down in tables, and through each widget's View Report link
At the top in the largest widget
Remove it from the org
Put it in every widget
questions.explain: Keep the top clean and let View Report and tables lower on the page carry the detail.

questions.q: A dashboard now has 25 widgets and viewers are lost. What is the best fix, per this lesson?
options: Make every widget the same size
Use a different color for every chart
Split it into two focused dashboards and trim to roughly six to ten widgets each
Add more text widgets
questions.explain: Modest widget counts and a single clear purpose per dashboard keep it readable.
